translations.text: He came as a witness, to testify about the light, so that everyone might believe through him.
He came to what was his own, and his own people did not receive him.
They asked him, “Why, then, do you baptize if you are not the Christ, or Elijah, or the prophet?”
He said to them, “Come, and you will see.” So they came and saw where he was staying, and they stayed with him that day. It was the tenth hour.
He said to him, “Everyone serves the good wine first, and when people have become drunk, they serve the inferior wine. But you have kept the good wine until now.”
Then the Jews said, “It took forty-six years to build this temple, and you will raise it up in three days?”
What is born of the flesh is flesh, and what is born of the Spirit is spirit.
Truly, truly, I tell you, we speak about what we know and testify about what we see, but you do not accept our testimony.
So that he may give everyone who believes in him eternal life in him.
You yourselves testify that I said, “I am not the Christ, but I was sent ahead of him.”
He must become greater, and I must become less.
He left Judea and went back to Galilee.
The woman answered, saying, “I have no husband.” Jesus said to her, “You were right to say, ‘I have no husband.’”
The woman said to him, “We know that the Messiah is coming, the one called the Christ. When he comes, he will tell us everything.”
They said to the woman, “We no longer believe because of what you said, for we have heard him ourselves, and we know that he truly is the Savior of the world.”
Immediately the man became well, picked up his mat, and walked. Now that day was the Sabbath.
Search the Scriptures, because you yourselves say that you have eternal life in them, and they are the ones that testify about me.
A large crowd was following him because they saw the signs he was performing on those who were sick.
Then Jesus looked up and saw that a large crowd was coming toward him. He said to Philip, “Where will we buy bread for these people to eat?”
Philip answered him, “A hundred staters’ worth of bread would not be enough for each of them to receive a little.”
Then Jesus took the loaves, gave thanks, and gave them to those who were reclining. Likewise, they received some of the fish.
Then Jesus said to them, “Truly, truly, I tell you, it was not Moses who gave you the bread from heaven, but my Father gives you the true bread from heaven.”
They were saying, “Is this not Jesus, Joseph’s son, whose father and mother we know? How, then, does he say, ‘I came from heaven’?”
But this is the bread that comes from heaven, so that anyone who eats of it will not die.
Then many of his disciples, when they heard this, said, “This teaching is hard. Who can listen to it?”
The Jews were amazed and said, “How is this man so learned without having been taught?”
For this reason Moses gave you circumcision—not that it comes from Moses, but from the ancestors—and you circumcise a man on the Sabbath.
Then they said to him, “How, then, were your eyes opened?”
They asked them, “Is this your son, whom you say you gave birth to blind? How, then, can he see now?”
Then Jesus said to them again, “Truly, truly, I tell you, I am the shepherd of the sheep.”
I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for his sheep.
Others said, “These are not the words of someone possessed by a demon. Can a demon open the eyes of the blind?”
But you do not believe because you are not among my sheep.
My sheep listen to my voice, and I know them, and they will follow me.
Many people went to him and said, “John performed no sign, but everything John said about this man is true.” And many believed in him there.
Then they removed the stone from there. Jesus lifted his eyes toward heaven and said, “My Father, I thank you because you have heard me.”
If we let him continue like this, everyone will believe in him, and the Romans will come and take away both our place and our nation.
They were looking for Jesus and said to one another as they stood in the temple, “What do you think? Will he not come to the festival?”
The chief priests and the Pharisees had given an order that if anyone knew where he was, they should tell them so that they could arrest him.
So that the words spoken by Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled: “Lord, who has believed our message? And to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?”
For this reason they could not believe, because Isaiah also said:
For they loved praise from people more than praise from God.
Jesus said to him, “Someone who has bathed needs only to wash his feet; otherwise he is completely clean. You too are clean, but not all of you.”
Peter said to him, “Lord, why can I not follow you now? I will lay down my life for you.”
Thomas said to him, “Lord, we do not know where you are going. How can we know the way?”
Believe me that I am in my Father and my Father is in me. If not, believe his works.
If you ask for anything in my name, I will do it.
Look, an hour is coming, and it has come, when you will be scattered, each to his own place, and you will leave me alone. Yet I am not alone, because my Father is with me.
I am not praying for these alone, but also for the others who will believe in me through their word.
Jesus said to Peter, “Put your sword into its sheath. Shall I not drink the cup that my Father has given me?”
Then Pilate took Jesus and had him whipped.
They kept coming up to him, saying, “Hail, King of the Jews!” and slapping him.
Then he said to the disciple, “Here is your mother.” From that day on, the disciple took her into his home.
He looked inside and saw the linen cloths lying there, but he did not go in.

On the evening of that Sunday, the doors of the place where his disciples had gathered were shut because they were afraid of the Jews. Jesus came and stood among them and said to them, “Peace be with you.”
He said to them again, “Peace be with you. Just as my Father sent me, I too am sending you.”
When morning came, Jesus stood on the shore, but the disciples did not know that it was Jesus.
Jesus said to them, “Little children, do you have any fish?” They answered him, “No.”
When they came ashore, they saw a charcoal fire with a fish on it, and bread lying there.
